problem: MLLM-based VLN models (NaVid, NaVILA, StreamVLN, NavFoM) need huge training compute because they process very long histories of dense visual tokens (quadratic cost), and DAgger with a fixed oracle/learned mixing ratio forces a trade-off between error-recovery exploration and trajectory length.
motivation: Training overhead (1,500 A100 / 4,032 H100 GPU hours for StreamVLN / NavFoM) prevents groups with limited compute from building VLN models. The two cost drivers are the history token count and the length of exploratory DAgger trajectories, so targeting both should give large savings without losing accuracy.
key_idea: Use a progressive spatially-compressed memory (or a KV-cache-based recursive memory) plus geometry-enhanced RGB features and a DAgger dynamic mixed policy whose oracle probability rises over the episode, giving a cheap yet SOTA RGB-only VLN model.
insight: Keeping recent frames at higher resolution while compressing older ones beats uniformly aggressive compression (3-frame progressive vs all-frame 4-token: +2.6 SR R2R-CE, +3.0 RxR-CE) and keeps improving with a longer window on long-horizon RxR-CE, while recursive KV memory is competitive on short R2R-CE but weaker on RxR-CE. The dynamic beta (learned policy early, oracle late) beats the best constant beta=0.25 in SR (60.8 vs 59.5 on R2R-CE) with far shorter collected trajectories (82 vs 128 steps), showing that errors are needed early but long wandering is wasted.
method: Geometry-enhanced visual representation: Qwen2.5-VL 2D tokens are added element-wise to StreamVGGT-1B 3D latent tokens (via 2-layer MLP) computed from RGB only with KV cache; random frame eviction bounds the cache.
Temporal sampling: frames sampled at stride Δ=4 to reduce redundancy.

Progressive memory: the K=3 most recent sampled frames are downsampled 2x2, the next K 4x4, and so on; total memory tokens are bounded by KS/3 (about one extra image); a sliding window of 12 frames is used by default.

Recursive memory: learnable tokens m_cur; their per-layer KV states at the previous step replace the placeholder m_pre KV at the current step, giving fixed-size memory with better gradient flow than hidden states (64 tokens in ablation).

Dynamic mixed policy for DAgger: oracle probability beta_t = 1 - alpha^(t/T) (alpha=0.5) so the agent starts with the learned policy and shifts toward the oracle. Expert labels are 4-step action chunks, and a single DAgger iteration is used.

Sequence packing: consecutive steps are flattened into one sequence with a block-sparse attention mask (Flex-FlashAttention). Steps per backward pass go from 8 to 16, cutting training cost by 41.2%, and gradients can flow across steps for recursive memory.
Two-stage training (following StreamVLN): stage 1 on R2R-CE + RxR-CE (no EnvDrop); stage 2 adds ScaleVLN-150K, ScanQA, SQA3D, a LLaVA-Video-178K subset, and DAgger data.

setting.training_data: R2R-CE and RxR-CE, DAgger trajectories (R2R 10.8K and RxR 19.7K), ScaleVLN-150K, ScanQA, SQA3D, LLaVA-Video-178K subset; about 3.7M state-action samples and 196K trajectories in total; 282 H800 GPU hours
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB only, 512x512, HFOV 90°, with history frames (no depth, odometry or panorama)
setting.action_space: discrete low-level actions (forward, left, right, stop); predicts 4 actions per step
setting.privileged: none at test time (the oracle policy is used only for DAgger data collection in training)

numbers.extra: trained with additional data external to Matterport3D (ScaleVLN-150K, QA and video data)
trained with additional data external to Matterport3D

numbers_note: The conclusion text states 62.3% SR on R2R-CE and 64.5% on RxR-CE, which conflicts with the abstract and Table 1 (64.2 / 67.0); the table values were used. Data-composition results are given only in a figure, but the text quotes 45.9 SR / 41.9 SPL for the stage-1 baseline. Appendix also reports SQA3D (Avg 56.2) and ScanQA (CIDEr 95.6), which are not navigation benchmarks.
results: Without external data, Efficient-VLN reaches 60.8 SR on R2R-CE and 63.5 SR on RxR-CE, beating StreamVLN (52.8 and 48.6). With ScaleVLN it reaches 64.2 SR / 55.9 SPL on R2R-CE and 67.0 SR on RxR-CE, ahead of StreamVLN† (56.9 / 52.9) and NavFoM† (56.2 / 57.4), using only 282 H800 GPU hours versus 1,500 A100 for StreamVLN and 4,032 H100 for NavFoM.
limitations: Recursive memory underperforms progressive memory on long-horizon RxR-CE, so the fixed-size state struggles to retain long-term information.
Only a single DAgger iteration is used, and evaluation is limited to simulated R2R-CE/RxR-CE with no real-robot tests.
The best results depend on extra data (ScaleVLN-150K); the paper's conclusion numbers are inconsistent with its abstract and tables.
